standard_prerequisites.name: Restriction to the localized category is both a left and a right adjoint
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Stacks Project, Modules on Sites, section on internal hom (adjointness of j_U^*)
standard_prerequisites.use: Gives preservation of limits by restriction, which the sectionwise computation needs.

core_obligations: For a diagram of presheaves G_i and an object U, use that the restriction functor j_U^* is both left and right adjoint, hence preserves limits: lim_i j_U^*G_i = j_U^*(lim_i G_i) (proof lines 4104-4107).
Compute the sections of the internal hom at U and apply the definition of a limit to obtain the displayed chain of equalities, proving statement (1) (proof lines 4108-4117).

Repeat the same computation for the second variable to prove (2), and deduce (3) for sheaves of modules from (1) using that limits of sheaves are computed in sheaves and that the sheaf internal hom is the sheafification of the presheaf one, up to line 4132.
proof_roadmap: Evaluate the internal hom at an object and use adjointness of restriction.
Apply the definition of a limit to conclude.
Transfer to sheaves via the presheaf computation.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that for presheaves of modules the internal hom functor commutes with arbitrary limits in either variable, and that the same holds for sheaves of modules. The proof takes a diagram of presheaves, evaluates at an object U, and uses that the restriction functor to the localized category is both a left and a right adjoint, so it preserves limits; the computation of sections of the internal hom then turns the claim into the defining property of a limit, and the second statement follows by the same computation (proof lines 4103-4132). The sheaf statement is deduced from the presheaf one because the limit of a diagram of sheaves is computed as a sheaf and the internal hom of sheaves is the sheafification of the presheaf internal hom. H2: the sectionwise computation using the two-sided adjointness of restriction is the substance.
